g9-civics-uc2-t1.overview: Digital technology is the use of computers, tablets, mobile phones and the digital and social media reached through them on the internet. This lesson defines the concept and shows how deeply daily life in Ethiopia now depends on it.
objectives: Explain the concept of digital technology
Identify common examples of digital technologies
Describe the need for digital technology in daily life activities
Trace the origin of digital technology to the mid-20th century
Recognise how digital technology supports communication, learning and finance in Ethiopia
g9-civics-uc2-t1.simple: Digital technology means using computers, tablets, mobile phones and the digital and social media that are reached through those devices on the internet. It also includes newer communication technologies that strongly affect political, economic, social and cultural life. Digital technology moves information and data quickly from one part of the world to another, and between individuals, through mobile applications, social media platforms and digital marketing websites. It began in the mid-20th century and is now the most significant modern technology in both developed and developing countries, including Ethiopia. Common examples are computers, smartwatches, ATMs, digital cameras, automated vehicles, drones, Bitcoin and GPS. In Ethiopia, fast communication, money transfer, banking and access to education are now impossible without it.
g9-civics-uc2-t1.detailed:
What digital technology is. Digital technology refers to the use of computers, tablets, mobile phones and the digital and social media that are accessed on those devices through the internet. The concept may also involve new communication technologies that can have significant effects on the political, economic, social and cultural life of societies. The textbook defines it more broadly as a type of technology used to transfer information and to move data quickly, including all electronic tools, automatic systems, technological devices and resources that generate, process or store information.

How it moves information. Digital technology plays a significant role in transferring information and data quickly from one section of the world to another and among individuals as well. This happens through mobile applications, social media platforms and digital marketing websites. Because huge amounts of information can be compressed onto small storage devices, it can be preserved and transported easily.

An age of dependence. Today we live in the age of digital technology, in which our life heavily relies on different types of technologies. Technology touches every aspect of our life, making it easier, better and life changing. Through social networks and social media platforms there is now high interconnection between individuals and global societies, and many people use electronic devices such as computers and mobile phones in their daily life.

Where it came from. Digital technology was started in the mid-20th century. It has now become the most significant modern technology, not only in developed countries but also in developing countries including Ethiopia. Its use and application are crucially important in day to day life, especially for communication speed, learning opportunities, social relations and money exchange in the finance sector.

Common examples. The most common digital technologies used today include the computer, smartwatch, Automated Teller Machine (ATM), digital camera, automated vehicles, drone, Bitcoin and GPS. These are everyday tools rather than distant inventions; a student in Addis Ababa and a shopkeeper in Hawassa may both use several of them before noon.

Digital technology in Ethiopia. In contemporary Ethiopia, easy and fast communication among individuals, money transfer, banking and access to education are impossible without digital technology. As digital citizens our individual life is highly dependent on modern digital media technologies. This may involve using a mobile phone to communicate with family members, using online services through the internet, and transferring money through mobile banking at any time. These technologies make life easier and better by saving the time and physical contact needed to get different kinds of services.

keyTerms.def: A type of technology used to transfer information and to move data quickly, including electronic tools, automatic systems, devices and resources that generate, process or store information.
Platform sites or spaces of multidirectional, instantaneous communication that operate using encoded machine-readable data formats.
The emerging human world dominated by the use of technology in modern life, driven and transformed by digitized information and communication technologies.
A computer-based technology that facilitates the sharing of ideas, thoughts and information by building virtual networks and communities.
A type of social media that helps users exchange thoughts, ideas and content, often with people who share tastes and interests.
A person who lives and takes part in daily life through modern digital media technologies such as mobile phones and the internet.
A digital service that allows money transfer and banking transactions at any time using a mobile phone.
The field of electronic devices and systems, such as computers and the internet, used to create, store and share information.

workedExamples.problem: A rural student says there is no need for digital technology in her daily life. Use the concept of digital technology to assess this claim.
workedExamples.given: Digital technology includes computers, mobile phones, tablets and the digital and social media reached through the internet.
workedExamples.formula: Rule: digital technology is the whole range of electronic tools and systems that generate, process, store and transfer information.
workedExamples.substitution: Even in rural areas, mobile phones are used for communication, mobile banking and market information.
workedExamples.calculation: Since the definition covers cheap mobile devices and not only computers, the claim does not hold.
workedExamples.answer: The claim is not correct; digital technology, especially the mobile phone, is already part of rural daily life.

workedExamples.problem: Ato Bekele sends money to his mother in Gondar from Addis Ababa at nine in the evening without travelling. Which use of digital technology does this show?
workedExamples.given: The transfer happens at any time and without physical contact.
workedExamples.formula: Principle: digital technology supports money exchange in the finance sector and saves time and physical contact.
workedExamples.substitution: Mobile banking transfers money between distant places almost instantly.
workedExamples.calculation: The service matches the described functions of money transfer and banking through digital technology.
workedExamples.answer: It shows money exchange through mobile banking, one of the key uses of digital technology.

workedExamples.problem: A school wants to show that communication speed matters for its results. Use the concept of digital technology to explain.
workedExamples.given: Email and social media platforms move information instantly across the world.
workedExamples.formula: Rule: digital technology transfers information and data quickly from one section of the world to another.
workedExamples.substitution: Teachers and students can share materials and results in seconds instead of days.
workedExamples.calculation: Faster exchange of information improves access to learning opportunities, so the claim holds.
workedExamples.answer: Digital technology improves communication speed and with it access to learning.

workedExamples.problem: A citizen argues that digital technology is limited to the internet. Correct the misunderstanding.
workedExamples.given: The textbook includes all electronic tools, automatic systems, devices and resources that generate, process or store information.
workedExamples.formula: Rule: digital technologies are ever present and are not limited to the internet or modern communication technologies.
workedExamples.substitution: An ATM, a digital camera and a GPS device are digital technologies that work beyond browsing the internet.
workedExamples.calculation: Applying the broad definition, the narrower claim fails.
workedExamples.answer: Digital technology is much broader than the internet; it includes many devices and systems used daily.

commonMistakes: Thinking digital technology means only the internet or only social media.
Believing digital technology is useful only in developed countries and not in Ethiopia.
Assuming a smartwatch or an ATM is not digital technology because it is not a desktop computer.
Treating digital technology as something that started recently rather than in the mid-20th century.
Ignoring the political, economic, social and cultural effects of new communication technologies.
Believing digital technology saves only money and not time and physical effort.
applications: Sending money to family in your home town through mobile banking.
Using a mobile phone to call and check on parents living in a rural kebele.
Using GPS on a phone to find a health centre in an unfamiliar town.
Withdrawing cash from an ATM in Addis Ababa instead of queueing inside a bank.
Using an online service to register for a national examination or a training course.
Using a digital camera to record a community event for a local school project.
g9-civics-uc2-t1.summary: Digital technology is the use of computers, tablets, mobile phones and the digital and social media reached through them, together with all electronic tools and systems that generate, process, store and transfer information. It began in the mid-20th century and is now the most significant modern technology in developed and developing countries alike, including Ethiopia. It supports communication speed, learning opportunities, social relations and money exchange, and makes daily life easier by saving time and physical contact.

g9-civics-uc2-t2.overview: Culture and technology are two equal forces that shape how we see the world. This lesson explains their interdependence, how digital media can promote Ethiopian culture, and how careless use can damage it.
objectives: Describe the relationship between culture and digital technology
Explain why culture and technology are interdependent
Examine the positive effects of digital technology on society's cultures
Examine the negative effects of digital technology on society's cultures
Demonstrate the responsible use of social media to promote Ethiopian culture
g9-civics-uc2-t2.simple: Culture and technology are two equal forces that greatly influence our attitudes, beliefs, behaviours and our understanding of good and bad. Society's cultures are the bases of human civilization and technological advancement, so cultural values and modern technologies are interdependent. When a new technology enters a society, the culture reacts either positively or negatively. Communication technologies let us share ideas and feelings, and through them culture is learned, transmitted and preserved. Digital platforms such as YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, Telegram and IMO can promote language, dress, food, arts, tourism sites and holidays to the world. But when used against our norms and moral values, digital technology can cause cultural diffusion and destroy indigenous values, for example by damaging family relationships.
g9-civics-uc2-t2.detailed:
Two equal forces. Culture and technology are the major factors that can shape our world outlooks. They are two equal forces that greatly influence our attitudes, beliefs, behaviours and our understanding of good and bad in different ways. Society's cultures are the bases of human civilization and technological advancement, which means that the cultural values of society and modern technologies are very interdependent.

How culture reacts. When new technologies are introduced into a society, the culture reacts in either a positive or a negative way. Cultural development and digital technologies are directly interlinked in terms of making one's culture accessible to others. The essential way to live in societies and to maintain one's culture is to communicate, through which cultural elements are shared.

Culture is learned and preserved through communication. Communication technologies are used to share ideas and feelings, and it is through them that culture is learned, transmitted and preserved. This enables us to promote our own cultural values and also to know the cultures of other societies. It is therefore difficult to promote and preserve one's own culture effectively without communication media in this digital world.

Promoting Ethiopian culture. Digital technologies are very crucial in highlighting the bright aspects of our country to the rest of the world. Ethiopia is a country of multicultural societies where different nations and nationalities have been living together for a long period of time, so all of them need to promote and preserve their cultures through different means. In this digital age it is important to use digital communication technologies such as YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, Telegram and IMO in a responsible and ethical way. We can promote the untold facts of our culture, such as language, way of life, cultural dressing, cultural food, arts, historical tourism sites and holiday celebrations, to other societies and across the world.

When use goes wrong. Digital technologies do not have only positive impacts on one's own culture. They have serious negative impacts if they are not used appropriately and in a responsible manner. Using such technologies in a way deviated from our norms or moral values and principles can lead to cultural diffusion and the destruction of the indigenous values and norms of a particular society. For example, the unit shows that inappropriate use of digital technology can affect family relationships when both husband and wife are too busy using social media at their meal and ignore their child.

The rule for a digital culture. Our digital culture must be in line with the existing moral, social and cultural values of the society in the contemporary digital age. The use and application of digital technology and media in day to day life must therefore be balanced with the values that hold families and communities together.

keyTerms.def: The shared way of life of a society, including its language, values, beliefs, customs, dress, food and arts.
The whole lifestyle and habits created by the innovations of the technological age, in which technology takes more place in daily life and shapes how we interact, behave, think and communicate.
The spreading or mixing of cultural elements between societies, which can weaken the indigenous values and norms of a particular society when it results from careless use of media.
The original moral and social standards of a particular society, which may be damaged by inappropriate use of digital technology.
The condition in which two things rely on and affect each other, as cultural values and modern technologies do.
An online service such as YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, Telegram or IMO used to share ideas, images and content.
A society made up of many nations, nationalities and cultures living together, such as Ethiopia.

workedExamples.problem: A young Ethiopian posts a video of a traditional coffee ceremony and viewers abroad ask about it. Analyse this using the relation between culture and digital technology.
workedExamples.given: The post shares a cultural practice with a global audience.
workedExamples.formula: Principle: communication technologies let culture be learned, transmitted and preserved, and can promote one's own culture.
workedExamples.substitution: The video carries a cultural element, the coffee ceremony, to societies that did not know it.
workedExamples.calculation: Sharing culture ethically promotes cultural values and teaches others, so the effect is positive.
workedExamples.answer: A positive effect: digital media promotes and preserves Ethiopian culture across the world.

workedExamples.problem: At dinner, both parents keep scrolling through social media and ignore their child. Interpret this example from the unit.
workedExamples.given: The use of digital technology is inappropriate within family time.
workedExamples.formula: Principle: use of digital media must be in line with the moral, social and cultural values of society.
workedExamples.substitution: Careless use replaces attention to family with attention to a screen.
workedExamples.calculation: Because the behaviour deviates from family values, it damages relationships, which is a negative cultural effect.
workedExamples.answer: It is a negative effect of digital media on family relationships, showing why use must follow cultural values.

workedExamples.problem: A group spreads foreign trends online while mocking local dress and language. Using the lesson, judge the effect.
workedExamples.given: The content rejects indigenous values and norms.
workedExamples.formula: Rule: use of digital technology deviated from our norms and moral values can cause cultural diffusion and the destruction of indigenous values.
workedExamples.substitution: Mocking local dress and language weakens those cultural elements.
workedExamples.calculation: The trend matches the description of cultural destruction rather than cultural promotion.
workedExamples.answer: A negative effect: it destroys indigenous values instead of promoting them.

workedExamples.problem: A regional culture bureau wants to promote historical tourism sites. Suggest a responsible digital method.
workedExamples.given: Ethiopia has many historical tourism sites and a multicultural heritage.
workedExamples.formula: Principle: use digital platforms responsibly and ethically to promote the untold facts of our culture.
workedExamples.substitution: Photos, short videos and accurate information can be shared on social media platforms.
workedExamples.calculation: This follows the code of responsible use while reaching the rest of the world.
workedExamples.answer: Use social media and other digital platforms responsibly to share accurate content about the sites and their culture.

commonMistakes: Believing culture and technology are unrelated rather than interdependent.
Assuming that all effects of digital media on culture are negative.
Thinking that only experts can promote a culture, not ordinary social media users.
Sharing content that mocks local language, dress or food as if it were harmless.
Letting social media replace attention to family members at meals and gatherings.
Assuming that anything posted online must be accepted simply because it is modern.
Believing culture can be preserved without any form of communication media.
applications: Posting a short video of a Timkat, Meskel or Ashenda celebration with an accurate explanation.
Writing a post that teaches a word from your mother tongue to other Ethiopians.
Sharing photos of Ethiopian cultural dress and food with correct names and descriptions.
Creating an online page that promotes a historical site such as Lalibela or Aksum to visitors.
Ignoring and reporting content that mocks the language or customs of another Ethiopian community.
Keeping family mealtimes free of phones so social media does not damage relationships.
g9-civics-uc2-t2.summary: Culture and technology are two equal forces that shape our attitudes, beliefs and behaviour, and the cultural values of society and modern technologies are interdependent. Communication media allow culture to be learned, transmitted and preserved, and digital platforms can promote Ethiopian language, dress, food, arts, tourism sites and holidays to the world. Yet when digital technology is used against our norms and moral values it causes cultural diffusion and destroys indigenous values, so our digital culture must stay in line with existing moral, social and cultural values.

g9-civics-uc2-t3.overview: Digital technology is used for the right purpose to make work efficient and effective. This lesson explains its four major purposes: social connection, communication speed, online learning and digital marketing.
objectives: Explain the major purposes of using digital technology
Describe how digital technology supports social connection
Explain how digital technology increases communication speed
Describe the online learning opportunities created by digital technology
Exhibit the benefits of digital marketing in the twenty-first century
g9-civics-uc2-t3.simple: Digital technologies are now part of our daily life, and many of us use laptops, tablets, mobile phones and the internet to get services easily, quickly and at low cost. Using digital technology for the right purpose helps us do our work more efficiently and effectively. The major purposes in the twenty-first century are social connection, communication speed, online learning opportunities and digital marketing. Social connection lets families, friends and remote workers communicate by words, video calls and media exchange. Communication speed lets huge amounts of data be compressed and moved instantly anywhere. Online learning gives access to courses, books and journals without going to a learning centre. Digital marketing promotes a business online through websites, applications and social media, so customers can buy even when the shop is closed.
g9-civics-uc2-t3.detailed:
Digital technology as part of daily life. Now-a-days digital technologies are part of our daily life activities. Many of us use digital technology such as laptops, tablets, mobile phones and the internet to get different services easily, quickly and cost effectively. Using digital technology for the right purpose helps us undertake our work more efficiently and effectively.

Social connection. Information is an indispensable factor in all aspects of our life. Connecting families, relatives and members of society at all levels is crucial for a healthy social life. Digital technology has simplified the process of socialization by enabling people to communicate with families, friends and team workers even when working remotely. This has made it possible to communicate through words, video such as video calls and virtual conferences, and exchanged media. Without digital devices and information communication technology, leading life is becoming very difficult these days.

Communication speed. Digital technology helps a large amount of information to be compressed on small storage devices that can be transported. The speed of the internet is constantly improving, enabling us to transfer tons of information instantly and to access data virtually anywhere in the world. It also improves the speed of transmission and has ultimately transformed the way people communicate, work and learn. Communication through digital technology lets global communities conduct speedy communication and information exchange in a fraction of a microsecond, which makes life on this earth better. For instance, without email it is very difficult for individuals and organizations to communicate between senders and receivers.

Online learning opportunities. In modern society people use digital media daily and seamlessly, and educators need to consider the integration of digital media today and for the future. By having access to the internet we can now reach different information within seconds just by searching online. Digital technology has made it possible for everyone to have access to things like online courses, training, books, journals, publications and other important information. The facilities of online education and the availability of interactive media have made the process of learning interesting, so learners can get an education without going to a learning centre.

Digital marketing. Digital marketing is another essential purpose of using digital media in business activities. It is the promotion of a business using online resources and tools such as websites, micro-sites, mobile applications and social media platforms. Using online selling, businesses allow customers to buy whenever they want, even when the shop doors are closed. Selling online typically helps reduce processing times internally, enabling the business to focus staff elsewhere, and gives customers access through whatever means they prefer: a mobile device, a desktop computer, a phone call or social media.

Why the purpose matters. In today's world technology serves a variety of purposes and means different things to different people, and the importance of digital technology has become integral in daily lives. As a result, without the use and application of digital technology, life in this digital world is difficult. To make our day to day life easier we must therefore use digital technology effectively and efficiently.

keyTerms.def: The promotion of a business using online resources and tools such as websites, micro-sites, mobile applications and social media platforms.
The use of digital technology to link families, relatives, friends and team workers, including through words, video calls and media exchange.
The rapid transmission of information and data made possible by constantly improving internet and digital networks.
Education delivered through the internet, giving access to courses, training, books, journals and publications without going to a learning centre.
The buying and selling of goods and services using mobile phones, tablets or other digital devices.
The process of interacting with others and building social relationships, which digital technology has simplified.
The storing of large amounts of information on small devices so that it can be preserved and transported easily.

workedExamples.problem: Megarsa Tullu, a farmer in the rural village of Dimtu, uses his mobile phone to learn market prices and inform other farmers. Which purpose of digital technology does this show?
workedExamples.given: A farmer uses a mobile application to obtain and share market information in a rural area.
workedExamples.formula: Principle: digital technology is used for social connection and for fast access to information.
workedExamples.substitution: The phone links him with markets and with other farmers far away.
workedExamples.calculation: Access to information and connection with others through a mobile device matches the purpose of social connection.
workedExamples.answer: It shows social connection and information sharing through digital technology, even in a rural area.

workedExamples.problem: A student in a small town cannot travel to a city but wants to study a computer course. How can digital technology serve the purpose of learning here?
workedExamples.given: The student has internet access but no nearby learning centre.
workedExamples.formula: Rule: online learning gives access to education without going to a learning centre.
workedExamples.substitution: Courses, books and journals can be reached online through interactive media.
workedExamples.calculation: Because the purpose of online learning is exactly this, the student can study remotely.
workedExamples.answer: The student can take the course online, one of the main purposes of digital technology.

workedExamples.problem: A small shop in Merkato wants more customers while its doors are closed at night. Apply the purpose of digital marketing.
workedExamples.given: The shop trades in a fixed place and during limited hours.
workedExamples.formula: Principle: digital marketing allows customers to buy whenever they want, even when the shop doors are closed.
workedExamples.substitution: An online page and a social media account would display and sell the goods at any hour.
workedExamples.calculation: Selling online reduces processing times and widens access, so the purpose is served.
workedExamples.answer: The shop should use digital marketing such as a website or a social media page for online selling.

workedExamples.problem: A health office must send a report to a regional bureau six hundred kilometres away before morning. Which purpose does digital technology serve?
workedExamples.given: Large information must move a long distance very quickly.
workedExamples.formula: Rule: digital technology increases communication speed and moves data instantly over long distances.
workedExamples.substitution: Email or a messaging application can transmit the report in seconds.
workedExamples.calculation: The quick, low-cost transmission matches the purpose of communication speed.
workedExamples.answer: It serves communication speed, which lets information travel long distances almost instantly.

commonMistakes: Using digital technology without a clear purpose and still expecting efficiency.
Believing social media is only for entertainment and not for social connection and work.
Assuming online learning is only for people who live in cities.
Thinking digital marketing means only advertising and not selling or serving customers.
Ignoring email and messaging as slow, when their speed is the very reason they are used.
Forgetting that the same platform can serve a good purpose or a harmful one depending on its use.
applications: Using a video call to join a family meeting when you cannot travel home.
Joining an online class or watching an educational video to prepare for examinations.
Reading online journals and publications for a school research project.
A family shop posting its products on social media so customers can order at night.
Using email to send a school report to an education office in another region.
Checking current market prices for coffee or teff on a mobile application before selling a harvest.
g9-civics-uc2-t3.summary: Digital technology is part of daily life and is used to get services easily, quickly and at low cost. Its major purposes in the twenty-first century are social connection, communication speed, online learning opportunities and digital marketing. Social connection links families, friends and remote workers; communication speed moves large amounts of data instantly across the world; online learning opens courses, books and journals without a learning centre; and digital marketing lets businesses reach and sell to customers at any time.

g9-civics-uc2-t4.overview: Using the right digital technology for the right purpose must be governed by ethical codes of conduct. This lesson presents the rules that guide responsible use of digital media.
objectives: Identify ethical codes of conduct for using digital technology
Explain the importance of ethical codes of conduct in digital media use
Describe the objective of using digital media responsibly
Apply the codes of conduct to real online situations
Demonstrate self-control against addictive use of digital media
g9-civics-uc2-t4.simple: Using the right digital technology for the right purpose efficiently and effectively is a burning issue in the current digital world. Using digital media in our day to day life must be governed by a set of ethical codes of conduct. This involves stating the objective of using digital media and properly identifying its advantages and disadvantages before we begin. The information on social media is broad and uncensored, so ethics and rules of conduct are needed for effective and efficient use. The codes include using digital media for good things such as solving community problems, learning from the information you receive, ignoring content that provokes political, religious or sexual violence, treating others as you want to be treated, respecting privacy and confidentiality, avoiding fake news and defamation, acknowledging mistakes, and avoiding addiction.
g9-civics-uc2-t4.detailed:
Why codes of conduct are needed. Using the right digital technology for the right purpose efficiently and effectively is the burning issue in the current digital world. Using digital media in our day to day life must be governed by a set of ethical codes of conduct. This involves the objective of using digital media and the proper identification of their advantages and disadvantages while using them. Therefore, before using the available social media and other digital technologies, we have to identify their benefits and potential challenges to our daily life.

Social media is broad and uncensored. The information and contents of social media are broad and uncensored, so there must be ethics and a code of conduct to be followed for effective and efficient utilization. Each social media platform serves a purpose that is unique, and our social media use strategy, content and ethics must be adapted accordingly. The codes are general rules and policies that are consistent with the high standard of ethics we uphold and that emphasize the value we place on trust and on treating all members of our community with respect.

Use it for good. The first group of codes concerns purpose. We should use digital media for good things, such as solving community problems through awareness creation on important issues. We should also use the information we get from digital media as an input to improve our knowledge, experiences and skills needed to improve our life. In this way digital technology becomes a tool for personal and community development rather than a source of harm.

Respect and protect others. A second group of codes concerns how we treat other people. We should ignore contents that provoke political, religious and sexual violence, and treat others as we want to be treated. We must respect privacy and maintain confidentiality. We should avoid remarks that may constitute defamation and avoid posts that degrade individual dignity. When we are wrong, we should acknowledge and correct our mistakes promptly.

Truthfulness online. A third group concerns truth. We must avoid posting, sharing and following fake news, and we should fight fake news using digital media by exposing the facts. Because unverified content spreads quickly, checking before sharing is itself an ethical duty and a service to the community.

Guard your time and relationships. A fourth group concerns self-control. We should avoid spending much more time on digital media unnecessarily, and we should use digital media in a way that cannot affect relationships among families and friends. Digital media must not be used in a way that affects our study and working times, and each of us should free ourselves from being addicted to its use.

Why it matters. Using the right digital technology for the right purpose effectively is a challenging issue in the current digital world, and the rules for the proper use of these technologies have a direct effect on our behaviour. The current use and application of digital technologies therefore needs the proper identification of their benefits and potential challenges for the effective utilization of digital media.

g9-civics-uc2-t4.summary: Using the right digital technology for the right purpose must be governed by a set of ethical codes of conduct, because social media content is broad and uncensored. g9-civics-uc2-t5.overview: Communication transfers and exchanges messages, and digital media has become the key strategy for making it effective. This lesson explains what effective communication is and how digital tools improve it.
objectives: Define communication and the effectiveness of communication
Evaluate the role of digital media in effective communication
Explain how cellular and satellite technology increased communication speed
Describe how computers and mobile phones improve communication and commerce
Analyse the case study of Megarsa Tullu, a farmer using a mobile phone
g9-civics-uc2-t5.simple: Communication is one of the most important ways to transfer and exchange messages and information in our relations with others. It is the art and technique of informing and influencing individuals and a large audience about important issues by scientific and ethical methods. The effectiveness of communication determines success or failure in achieving individual and collective goals, and digital media has become the key strategy for it. Today organizations and individuals have some online presence through social media accounts, online networks, databases and email. Cellular and satellite technology increased communication speeds and made connection easier; the internet allows easy exchange of information over long distances; computers improved the storage and presentation of information; and mobile phones enabled e-commerce. The case of farmer Megarsa Tullu shows how a mobile phone brings market prices and national news to a rural village.
g9-civics-uc2-t5.detailed:
What communication is. Communication is one of the most important ways to transfer and exchange messages and information in our relations with others. It is the art and technique of informing and influencing individuals and the large audience about important issues in scientific and ethical methods. The effectiveness of communication determines the success and failure of individual and collective goal achievement.

Digital media as the key strategy. Digital media has become the key strategy for effective communication. Today, organizations and individuals have some type of online or digital presence through social media accounts, online networks and databases, and emails, in order to communicate with the public. There are various digital technologies which make use of the fastest growing information communication technology that we use to make communication effective, and this has improved businesses and personal communication. Successful modern organizations also use digital media to their advantage and to achieve effective communication.

Cellular and satellite technology. The contribution of digital media to effective communication has improved because cellular technology and satellite communication have increased communication speeds and made connection easier. A person can now reach someone across the country or abroad in seconds rather than through a slow chain of offices.

The internet and computers. The internet has enabled easy exchange of information over long distances and access to a web page server in some far-off country. Computers have enabled better storage and presentation of information and have made the process of teaching easier and more effective. Together they change not only how quickly we send a message but also how well it is organised and understood.

Mobile phones and e-commerce. Mobile phones have enabled e-commerce by giving customers the option to transact via their mobile phones or tablets and to perform specific tasks. This extends effective communication into buying and selling, so communication and commerce now work together.

Case study: Megarsa Tullu. Megarsa Tullu is a farmer living in a small village called Dimtu in a rural area. Using his mobile cell phone, he easily gets information about the market prices of some agricultural products. He used to get updated information about the price of locally produced agricultural commodities and inform it to other farmers. In addition, he is a well-informed person about what is going on in the country as a whole by effectively using important applications on his mobile cell phone. His case shows that effective communication through digital media is not limited to cities or to educated professionals; it reaches farmers and strengthens the whole community.

Digital media has become the key strategy for effective communication through social media accounts, online networks, databases and emails. Cellular and satellite technology increased the speed and ease of connection, the internet made long-distance exchange easy, computers improved the storage and presentation of information, and mobile phones enabled e-commerce. The case of farmer Megarsa Tullu shows how a mobile phone brings market prices and national news to a rural village.

g9-civics-uc2-t6.overview: Digital and social media are not used only for good; they also bring serious challenges. This lesson examines disregard for ethical values, fake news, and threats to privacy and security.
objectives: Identify the major challenges faced while using digital media technologies
Explain how disregard for ethical values harms digital communication
Describe the fabrication of fake news and its effects
Explain personal privacy and security risks in social media
Distinguish the advantages and disadvantages of social media for students
g9-civics-uc2-t6.simple: Using digital technologies and social media platforms is becoming challenging. Many of these challenges are related to social media because it is an internet-based platform. Social media such as Facebook has drawbacks like decreasing academic performance, negatively affecting performance in the workplace and causing problems in personal relationships. The main challenges are disregard for ethical values, fabrication of fake news, and personal privacy and security issues. Because the accuracy of information is not controlled, harmful and false content can spread widely and quickly. Fake news is used to manipulate public opinion for political or commercial gain, and privacy is hard to maintain because social media platforms are public. In the present day security issues have even become challenges to state national security.
g9-civics-uc2-t6.detailed:
Why digital media is challenging. Currently, using digital technologies and social media platforms is becoming challenging. Many of these challenges are related to social media because social media is an internet-based platform. Social media such as Facebook has many drawbacks, such as decreasing academic performance, negatively affecting performance in the workplace and causing problems in personal relationships. Digital technology and social media platforms may be used not only for better or good, but also for worse.

Disregard for ethical values. Ethics in digital media involves the moral problem associated with the adoption of new communication technologies in daily activities. The major concern in the ethics of digital media is the effect of the information that is transmitted through these channels. The big challenge is that the accuracy of the information is not controlled, and at times it can cause various impacts on society. Therefore, to use social media effectively in our day to day life we have to use digital technology ethically and in an appropriate manner.

Fabrication of fake news. In times of digital information exchange, fake news has become more of an online phenomenon that is difficult to control, and the sharing of fabricated news to shape public opinion has become a common phenomenon. Fake news can reach high levels of visibility in a short amount of time because it is easy to share via social media. It involves reports, images and videos that are shared to purposefully spread misinformation, that is, information that is factually incorrect. Fake news is mostly used to manipulate public opinion for political or commercial gain, to attract people to click through to linked websites and generate advertising income. Fake news and misinformation are therefore a common problem across all social media platforms.

Personal privacy and security issues. The most challenging aspect of using social media is privacy and security, about which users are very much worried. It is very difficult to maintain privacy in social media since these are public platforms and anyone can easily access the personal information of others. As a result, protecting individual privacy and keeping information confidential is at risk in the age of digital technologies. For example, when an individual posts and uploads information about his or her private life on Facebook and YouTube, someone could share it publicly so that anyone can see it. In the present day, security issues have become challenges to state national security as well.

Weighing advantages against disadvantages. The unit invites students to list the advantages and disadvantages of using social media for learning. On the advantage side, social media can help to prepare students for their learning. On the disadvantage side, the presence of social media can be distracting to students. Recognising both sides is the first step to using digital media responsibly.

Conclusion. In the present day, digital technologies have become indispensable tools that give users quick and fast communication. However, using these digital devices and social media platforms is hindered by different challenges, and inappropriate use of social media may lead to ethical violations, of which disregard for ethical values is one. Understanding these challenges is what allows a citizen to use digital media for better and not for worse.

g9-civics-uc2-t6.summary: Digital technology and social media are indispensable for quick communication, but they are also used for worse and not only for better, and they bring serious challenges. The main challenges are disregard for ethical values, because the accuracy of transmitted information is not controlled; the fabrication of fake news, which spreads misinformation quickly to manipulate public opinion for political or commercial gain; and personal privacy and security issues, since social media platforms are public and private information is easily accessed. Inappropriate use may even become a threat to state national security.
